title: Clopen restriction preserves the objectwise residue Tor interval
statement: Fix the prime l, finite coefficient extension E, scheme T, clopen open U and normalized datum d [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-pc-scheme, def-weil-open-immersion, def-sf-clopen-restriction-data]. Let M be any completed-coefficient derived object and a,b arbitrary integers. If its exponent-one derived reduction [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] has Tor amplitude [a,b] after restriction to every global pro-etale site object [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], then the exponent-one reduction of sfClopenDerivedRestriction d applied to M has the same Tor amplitude on every object of the component site. No completeness or tensor comparison data is asserted.

source.place: Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude; pro-etale slice relocalization and Tag 06YY, as expanded in lem-sf-clopen-derived-compatibility.

proof.text: Apply sf_clopen_scalar_quotient_comparison at exponent zero (the exponent-one quotient) to identify scalar reduction after clopen restriction with finite-coefficient restriction after global scalar reduction.

For V on the local pro-etale site put W equal to its composite object on T. Compose Over.post of the inclusion with sliceEquiv at W: this composite is definitionally the sliceEquiv functor at V. Cancellation of equivalences shows that Over.post is an equivalence. It is also continuous and cocontinuous. Pull d.finite 0 to the slice; the induced module restriction F is an additive equivalence, by the inverse site equivalence and inverse ring isomorphism. Cocontinuity and invertibility of the ring map give F its ordinary tensor comparison.

Use the derived tensor comparison for an additive tensor equivalence, specialized to a module in degree zero. Every local test module L is isomorphic to F(N). Exactness of F identifies homology of the derived image with F of homology. The global Tor test at W therefore gives zero local homology outside the same interval. Keep the ordered-interval conjunct unchanged.

The ordinary functors restricting to W and then along the slice equivalence agree with clopen restriction followed by restriction to V. Apply the exact-functor derived composition isomorphisms, then the scalar-reduction comparison from the first step. Tor amplitude is invariant under an isomorphism of its input since derived tensor and homology are functors. This proves the required objectwise bound for every V, including empty objects and the impossible ordered-interval premise when a>b.

lean.statement:
theorem sf_clopen_preserves_residue_tor
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] (T : Scheme.{t}) (U : T.Opens)
    (hU : IsClosed (U : Set T)) (d : SfClopenCoefficientRestriction l E T U) :
    ∀ (M : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E T)) (a b : ℤ),
    SfResidueTorAmplitudeOnEveryObject (l := l) (E := E) T
      ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E T 0).obj M) a b →
    SfResidueTorAmplitudeOnEveryObject (l := l) (E := E) U.toScheme
      ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E U.toScheme 0).obj
        ((sfClopenDerivedRestriction d).obj M)) a b
